# Preface

Hello my dear sibling, I am your sibling, Sidharth, I am the writer of this book; "Brothers, Sisters". So here I will showcase you this book as a brother. You can call me whatever you want. Thank you for supporting my last book in this series and it is also my first book named, "The Hidden Power Of Discipline". I hoe that you will enjoy this journey, I am writing it as a part of the series called; "The Path To A Meaningful Life". In this book we are going to uncover, discover, and findout the hidden secret of our sibling relations, how we can avoid fights, how we can end fights, and even how we can recover the situation you and your sibling lived before the fight. So I hope you, that you will like this journey and you will implement these qualities in you also, I usually write these types of "short-but-strong" guides, so I just hope that you will like this book. I have also programmed a website myself and I have published it in GIT Hub and opened it in github.io so I will also give its link in the about the author section, at the last page.

So, I hope you that you will like this journey.

[[PAGE_BREAK]]

# PART I
# THE WORLD WE LIVE IN

[[PAGE_BREAK]]

# Chapter I
# Fights We Don't Understand

"The truth of the problem..."

Have you ever wondered about the real problem in the fight with your sibling? Actually, there is no real truth about the problem between siblings, my dear sibling, consider the fight as a tomato soup, a soup made of a variety of ingredients from which the mains are; misunderstanding tomatoes, emotional corns, and the mix of expectations on others and scare of being less loved veggies. This soup is a bit more terrible then we imagine, it can cause long-term problems in understanding each others, and this simple thing is so important that if this soup was drank the effects can remain for a long time causing they break between siblings more... Normally time heals wounds but this soup is different, time heals wound that are in the table of healing in the book of time, but this soup is not in the that session it is located in the mix-up book of time and life. Actually, this soup is the test of our relationship, if we try to understand that situation a little bit, we had already passed $3/4$ of this test, leading to strengthen relations, love, affection, care of each other and so on. This truth of problem is these fights is that there is no actual problems in the scenario, the all cause of fights between sibling are only a little bit misunderstanding, a small sink hole of mud caused by a small rain of misunderstanding, which then slowly slowly leads to the crack of surface, a big crack caused by a little rain happened years ago. So, can this big crack can be dumped? ---Yes! But this is not easy as we think. My sibling, stop reading and imagine, imagine that in the place where you live had a sudden stroke of earthquake, an earthquake that had caused a big!-big!-big! crack in the whole surface! This great sized crack can take as many Statue Of Liberty(s) as many we can imagine! So, now I want to ask you that ---Can you can dump this? ---My answer, very-very tough job, better to quit, but yes, of course, I will try at my best before quitting, and if my mind and heart come together, it will succeed in no extra time! So for you what? Will you directly quit or try at your best for your sibling? Like dumping this crack in real world can cost a great amount of money, this also can cost!

Always remember....
....Dumping The Crack = Great Amount Of Money = A Very-Great Amount Of Hard-Work = Mind, Soul, Body and Heart should work together.

"Solution?"

So, is there any solution to degrade this soup? ---It is possible, we can avoid such soups, actually we needs skills to degrade this soup. On these skills the main and the most important one is patience! Just wait a minute and imagine; You were studying, suddenly your mother called you for some help, you quickly closed your books and went to your mother, after it you went to study when you found that your book is missing from the place where you had kept it before! You rushed to your sibling as she/he was the only person in the room where you were studying, you started asking her/him where is your book? She said she hadn't taken it, and slowly-slowly that debate became fight, hearing your both's voice your mother came to you searched for the book and found it on the table, the truth was that when you were going to your mother, you had accidently dropped your book under the table; and after it your sibling started teasing you, ---🕊"Huh? Look, who had dropped the book under the table and suspected that me had dropped it!" ---And this fight continued, but if you, if you had searched for your book where your were studying, and didn't rush to your sibling asking him or her to give your book, this soup shouldn't be drank!

My sibling, you should understand....
....The fight is not caused by the real problem it's caused by misunderstanding through impatience.

"At The End..."

At the end of this chapter, I will like to conclude that; the fight between siblings are not caused upon the real problems, it's caused on a little rain of misunderstanding which was formed upon the evaporation and the condensation of impatience. This little rain sometimes lefts a small muddy pad which slowly-slowly starts to eat the good habits that we do to our siblings, leading our siblings to see only the bad things we do to them even if its small thing, and then this small little muddy sink hole slowly - slowly grows to a big and great sized crack in the relationships of siblings, and as I said earlier, this great sized crack can take a lot of hard work, which is the phase where most people quit, but if we be careful, if we just be a little patient, the soup will automatically degrade; And even if the fight is going on, you can stop it by just stop building the fight again and again. The fight between siblings has a battery, when this battery's energy becomes low the fight eventually starts ex-tinting, but the problem in it is that we start building this fight again, like we are charging the battery of that phone that we don't like. Like when you had got your book, your mind was like; "OK. It's not his/her fault its mine!". In this situation, the fight in it starts draining its energy, then suddenly your sibling gave the boost; "How did you even dare to suspect me to hide your book.", now this battery starts charging and your mind also becomes angry! And this cycle followed until you stop to building it. My sibling you must understand, your sibling can't keep charging your fight's battery, a sound doesn't occurs from a clap if it is clapped by only one hand, if a clap is done by one hand, we can't even call it a clap!

Remember....
....If you want to stop the fight, firstly you should stop building the fight again and again, when the building of fight starts falling down don't go to help them building it again!

[[PAGE_BREAK]]

# Chapter II
# The Blame Game

"Rules;..."

So, what is a blame game? ---This time, I am sorry, I will not give answer for this question; ---Just ask yourself! What's a the blame game of you and your sibling(s)? I haven't told the answer because the answer is not a single it's like the game of cards everyone has their own rules and I don't want any creative differences between us. But the base game is same; cards! Playing happily in the rain of misunderstanding, then by just a mistake we hit our sibling and then in that same way a battery gets summoned and the same cycles continues, then the game starts; "Why did you hit me?", "I didn't you had!", and this blame game continues in this way. Actually this game is repeating session of mis-pointing each other that they hadn't did the wrong thing and their sibling had. This game can be caused upon a variety of things like tension, fight, and mainly on impatience + misunderstanding. And this blame game is the common cases of a foundation; The raw lithium of lithium li-ion battery of the fight! This strong foundation builds fight quickly and strongly, cause of the game normal fight can be more stronger and even some long term fights are only on blaming each other and teasing! Look, this much of problems can be only built upon the blaming cycle or the blame game!

My sibling....
....Want to end a fight? ---Just try to stop blaming or teasing your sibling!

"Round, Round Cycle"

As I had said this blame game is a repetitive session of blaming each other or mis-pointing each other that one is the good child and other is the bad child. This game is very toxic for sibling relations. It can break relations in a hazardous way. Escaping becomes impossible! Then how to avoid this cycle? ---The answer might change but the core is always same, ---Be calm! Your sibling can tease you, blame you on nothing but you should keep calm to handle that situation to break the battery, to end the cycle. My sibling, the blame game is not harm to you and your sibling's relation if you keep calm and treat it as nothing important to focus. Actually a research says that the blaming cycle is a defence mechanism usually summoned from fears; fears of being underestimated, less respected, being avoided etc... Imagine for a minute; Ramu is an office worker, he had a presentation that he wasn't able to complete in the given time ---not because he was lazy but the time given to complete the presentation was not enough. On the submission day, he was summoned to boss, with his employ friends as his work was divided with his friends, although he was the main leader in-charge of the project. His boss scolds him and his friends now from the fear of loosing his chance to promotion his inner defence mechanism activates, he says; "Boss! This is not my fault!", he points to one of the employ; "He was the one who divided his division is the main problem!", that one employ shouts back; "BOSS! HE IS A LIAR, I had already said that I am not for it but...", he points on another employ; "he was the one who convinced everybody and forced me to do the division!", now this cycle continues one employ shouts at other and other shouted at another! But the real problem was neither the division nor the lack of supervision from Ramu. The real cause was the lack of proper time! See how blaming works but don't think this only works on employment, it works on every scenario where a person has a partner to complete a task and when those people fail; they don't try to find the real root cause, but they fight and blame each other from the fear of loosing the reward!

Remember....
....The blame game is the game of cards but that doesn't mean it is played upon cards!

"At The End..."

So at the end of this chapter; I would like to conclude that, the blame game can have a variety of rules; but the game of cards is the game of cards not the game played on boards and while this game can bend its rules very-very much! But still its the game of cards it the game played in boards so its base is one in all the house; blame another one so you can survive! Make some stories or tell the true ones but do be careful from your mistakes from being presented against the court. Blame your sibling without even thinking about the root problem; if you want to permanently get rid of grass and unwanted weeds, you should try to remove the root of it, not the leaves! The round-round cycle of blame game varies but the foundation is strong and structured and is also simple rto avoid if you really want to!

So, the question is....
....Are you really ready to avoid it?

[[PAGE_BREAK]]

# Chapter III
# The Silence Between Us

"The darkness..."

The most dangerous apart of the fights between siblings is that as the fight grows a quite deep dark silence also starts t form. Slowly, slowly it starts to eat the energy to talk to the other siblings. The darkness slowly spreads as the fight grows more dangerous. This type of silence can be very toxic for the sibling relationship. The more the fight grows, the more the anger grows, and the more the relation breaks; causes this deep, dark silence to grow slowly-slowly... As I already said this silence is the most annoying and mysterious part in the fight between sibling relationship. This silence makes talking to other sibling likely impossible! It breaks relation from its root; it breaks it from the inner heart making the fight very strong and durable and making the relation at a point of end. It can tear sibling relations.

But....
....Do we have a chance?

"Solution..."

So, the good part in this is the solution is actually in a neutral part; it is hard and also easy it depends on the amount of silence and the time that have spend in this fight. The solution is also hidden in its name; silence... As the only solution of avoiding ad disappearing this silence is confession, confession of the truth, confession that you are also sad with this fight, that you also want to end this fight! You should try and try. Because the situation is neutral, sometimes it can be in the hard situation. The only way to make this situation easy, is to try-try and try! As you try continuously, your sibling understands your feelings and becomes softer with you to confess with you, understand you, and listen you from his/her heart. Thus making the situation also requires patience. Hence patience is one of the most valuable skills in our whole life, by the way.

Remember....
...Breaking silence can be as simple as slicing butter while it can also be as hard as cutting rocks!

"At The End..."

At the end of this chapter, I would like to conclude that; the silence between siblings is very confusing to be post graduated on! By the way our focus should be in solving it! The important part is that the silence can be disappeared by using confession, the truth, the truth that you want to also end the fight, that you are also not satisfied from it! My sibling, the human brain can be changed it's no a solid rock, its not a strict code, its not a strict behaviour, its human mind! For example; think of a time when two siblings are fighting, arguing on a topic that the number they are seeing is 6 or 9. The first sibling in it is Sib and second sibling is Sab. So how would you manage it, how would you understand them if it were your siblings? Hmmm... The answer might be position changing; you will ask them to change their position and then look at the image/number so they can understand the other sibling's meaning that why were they arguing which slowly-slowly can make sense in their mind, and then, they can slowly-slowly understand that its on the perspective of one! Ok, if your answer was similar so then that's good, it means that you understand the difference between one's and other's observation correctly, but if you didn't know then its also fine as you now understand what's perspective difference! But, but, but; What if the siblings where stubborn, stubborn to prove they are right and the other one is wrong; they are on a situation sticked to; "No Cuts, No buts, No Coconuts!", it means that they don't want any excuses, there are not going to listen anything they know what is right and wrong (in their perspective)! Then what will you do? The answer might be changed this time. --Quiting or Trying! Yes, this thing is true that if somebody is sticked to something then it will be a very-very big problem to solve it, nearly impossible but not proper impossible. The human mind is bendable, it can chance mood so if you try and try their mind will start to understand you, thus giving the permission to even look at the image inverted from their perspective!

Remember....
Each window has its own shade!

[[PAGE_BREAK]]

# PART II
# WHAT YOU CAN DO NOW

[[PAGE_BREAK]]

# Chapter IV
# Fixing Things Without Ego

"The power of words; I'm sorry..."

As a brother I know that, how difficult is saying sorry in between a serious fight... And not from any random phrase; "I'm sorry!" I meant sorry from the apologise that comes from our true heart when we really want to end the fight! This can be very difficult in that situation especially when your sibling is really mad at you and often when you also are mad at him/her! That means that you shouldn't be thinking she/he should apologise first not me, she had done the wrong thing then why should I apologise her/him? So, first you should clean up your mind the most important and the most of the problems of saying sorry comes from this step, cleaning our own mind first! So, after cleaning up your mind you will be able to understand the real problem; the root cause, and be able to think that why would had your sibling had fighted with you? My sibling, the reason why it feels very heavy to say sorry from our heart or a real apologise is because in our mind somewhere we still think she/he is wrong not me, your mind feels that yo shouldn't apologise first your sibling should! Why should you apologise? Think for a minute of your recent or last fight; what was the real problem in it? Had you been able to say sorry at least after your sibling had said? Are you feeling bad for that fight? Was it really our problem? And at least had you been able to think to apologise your sibling? Keep this questions in your mind.

Remember....
....Next time when you found yourself in a fight, ask yourself these questions to clean your mind!

"Importance..."

So, what is the importance of fixing things without ego? The answer is pretty simple; ---If you want to end a fight, you should first clean your mind clearly, so you can understand the fight, from its root to its stem and leaves as we should be able to findout why had this fight began, why is it continuing and does it seem to have any end in this fight? I meant that if your sibling also want to end this fight or he/she wants to continue. The importance of fixing things without ego is very important as it is the core that can only end a fight fully forever, so that no pain or regret is left behind this fight, the fight should only be a memory of sibling relation in you and your sibling's mind! My sibling, understand, that if you have ego and then you also want to end he fight it's likely because you are loosing in this fight as ego will never allow you to completely end a fight fully! Ending a fight with ego is like you are the villain and you are fighting with a hero and you just got frightened and you said maybe ending this fight would be good, to the hero. But not truly from heart, only from greed mind and a thought to revenge! You will never be able to end a fight truly and fully from the both sibling's mind and your mind! You will always keep a revenge feeling or a great fail feeling with ego in your mind! My sibling, do you remember the questions that I gave you in the last passage to clean your mind, to make a feeling that you want to end this fight from its root? Actually n it; it's not compulsory to answer that question in right middle of a fight, but remember it will do its thing!

So....
Are you the villain saying let's end this let's end this fight to the hero?

"At The End..."

So, at the end of this fight chapter, I will like to conclude that it's okay to feel difficult to say sorry from true heart. It's actually kinda good that you can you can find that you are in a situation in which you are not able understand and are feeling difficult to apologise as it shows that your ego has started reducing in your mind and you have started to slowly slowly understand the fight, it's the situation when your mind finally reaches out for an answer or the truth and when you get this knowledge acquired, you will slowly-slowly start to reflect your thoughts and will want to end this fight truly!

Remember....
....The moment when you realise that you are finding difficulty in saying sorry, is the moment when your brain starts the journey to end the fight!

[[PAGE_BREAK]]

# Chapter V
# Talking Again

"As the silence goes..."

As I have mentioned in the chapter; The Silence Between Us: The key factor to avoid silence is talking together both you and your sibling. In this chapter, we will explore this topic more deeply. My sibling, actually after a serious fight things don't go as expected, silence becomes very obvious, it slowly-slowly starts to revive the last fight. After a series fight, it's very important to start talking again and making an atmosphere where you and your sibling can talk again. Actually talking is more important than we expect. Take some time and imagine; If the World War III had just ended. Fortunately, Everybody was save. But then, what? What would you be able to do? Think little deeply, your schools are destroyed, your parent's job has destroyed, stock market wet down, farms where destroyed, groceries where out of supply, and the army was recovery and the government was unable to send army to your spot, to support and give a source of food, clothes and shelter. In this case, what would you be able to do? Slowly-slowly, will become worser. Some people will help others to survive and others will choose their own path. So, what's your choice? Would you choose to help others with a 70%-80% chance to survive would you rather choose to stay alone with a 20%-30% survival? Most of the people of other regions would think; "Oh! What a fortune! The war has ended! Everything is now fine!" But only you and your people would understand the problems that would come ahead.

So....
....Now, do you understand the after effects of a fight?

"Making things okay..."

So how to make things okay? Actually talking again is the key to make things normal again as when a fight ends, it lefts behind some memories, so, it's important to fix things in hat stage, then comes making everything normal, so that, you and your sibling doesn't contain any bad memory from that fight. A fight is normal in sibling relationships, but it becomes very dangerous when siblings start to stop talking to each other, the silence starts to make talking feel more uncomfortable and unworthy. In simple terms, it kills sibling relations. But still there's a chance, a chance to make things okay.

So....
....Will you try to make things okay?

"At The End..."

At the end of this chapter, I will like to conclude that, when a war ends people from other regions think; oh the war ended, now everything will be fine! But only the people who have suffered would only understand the pain, that the war had left. A fight never ends peacefully, if you don't make it peaceful! People have different perspectives and only a few people reach out to understand others. For others, everything is fine, but the responsibility to make everything truly fine is upto you!

Remember....
....You are the person who should stabilise you and your sibling's relationship after a fight!

[[PAGE_BREAK]]

# Chapter VI
# Being The Better One First

"It actually means..."

So, what is the importance of being the better one first? Actually, it's a pretty simple question with a simple answer. So, what is the importance of being the better one first? Ask it to yourself, what does this sentence mean to you? As we said, it's simple. Yes, reading this line can be weird sometimes, but if you're commited to end a fight truly, by ending its bad memory etc... If you are commited to make things okay again, to make things normal again you should probably be able to accept that you should do it! It sounds easy, but it's not. Being better one first, means to avoid all of your sibling's bad stuffs and only focus on your sibling's good habits, no matter even if your sibling tries to break your limit, the limit of toleration. You should be able to tolerate your sibling completely.

Do you understand....
....Is it easy or difficult to you?

"How can I?...

Actually sometimes, it sounds weird to "be the better one first", but it's actually important than we think, or else you will found yourself keep charging the battery of the fight. It's easy to do, you know, but it can feel weird also if the fight was important to you, but if you don't help yourself to just do this simple thing, you cannot exit a fight, the root of that fight becomes you! And if the problem is you, then you can solve it easily but only when you understand that it's truly you, because to get out of this root thing, you should try to become the better one first. When we become the better one first, we are typically improving our nature towards our siblings, which helps us to exit from becoming the root cause of the problem. My sibling, becoming the better one first means to say sorry in a fight when saying it feels likely impossible, and even it works well, if you are the problem of the fight.

Remember....
....If you are the problem of the fight, and feel difficult to say sorry to your sibling, remember that there are another ways also to say sorry to your sibling.

"At The End..."

At the end of this chapter, I will like to conclude that, Being the better one first doesn't mean to show off something, make fun of your sibling or use it as a weapon to tease your sibling. It is the hidden act of saying sorry even in times when saying it feels impossible, unworthy, and uncomfortable. There isn't any importance to a sorry which is said from a rock heart, importance is given towards the sorry which is given from a true heart, and it also doesn't mean that you want to say it! There are another ways of saying it even without opening your mouth. The true sorry, or an apology lies in its kindness and truth, the kindness that you are using as your key to apology and the truth that you are really admitted to be careful next time with the mistake you did. Sorry doesn't mean just "sorrrrryyyyy..." but it means that I apologise to you for the mistake I made and I would be careful next time. It means that you are trustworthy to that person and will not repeat what happened.

So....
....Being the better one first doesn't mean that you should act like your better and worthy to your parents, it means to be kind towards your sibling as an apology for your mistake.

[[PAGE_BREAK]]

# Chapter VII
# The Bond That Never Breaks

"Recovering..."

So, have you ever heard that, sibling's bond are the one of the strongest bond in the world? I think most of us would have probably heard about it and actually it is also true that sibling relations never breaks. And from "never breaks" I doesn't mean they never apart, actually they do, but I meant that, their bonds recover, they recover faster than most of the bonds in our whole life we make. It's easier to recover a sibling bond. But it also doesn't mean that its easier than slicing a slice of butter! Siblings understand each other from a very young age and that makes them easier to recover from the stresses made from fights. Many people believe good siblings doesn't fight, but its not true, siblings are children, and among children misunderstandings often take place. As the old quote goes; "Real friends are not the one pair that doesn't fight, they fight, argue, but they don't do this for harming each other they argue when one friend is making a wrong decision". Siblings also fight, and this fact is often considered wrong sometimes, which is very harmful.

Remember....
....Real bonds also fight!

"Helping..."

So typically we have almost reached the end of this book but we didn't talked about what is the power of helping in recovering bonds! So a simple question, what is its actual power, because if you have tried the "Being The Better One First" method, you would have known that it play a large importance in it. Helping shows kindness, and kindness show that you are actually caring not just acting, it actually means a way of saying thank you towards your sibling, and this is an important thing itself, most of you have heard that eyes speak faster than words, but it also applies for our actions, our actions go/hit deeper than words, our actions say when we are even feared to open our mouth and our actions shows our kindness towards our sibling. Like if being the better one first is an example of showing your act of apology then helping your sibling is the act of showing your sibling the kindness you have for him/her, actually helping is the alternative word for "Thank you" in the language of the universe.

Always remember....
....An action/act is a representation of the words in literature in the "language of the universe".

"At The End..."

At the end of this chapter I will like to conclude that helping doesn't just mean an english literature word; it is the word of the language of the universe. In this world of cruelty the helping is the key to "on" the torch in your darkest hours in the sibling relations. My sibling, sometimes you can't open your mouth in the fights, sometimes you are afraid that you will cause your sibling feel more bad/sad, these are the conditions you need to understand the language of the universe, it's easy to learn it and once you learn it you will never forget it fully and neither it will become useless over time. The only thing you need to know to learn this art or language is it can be learnt by just experimenting, and/or experiencing what people thin to certain body languages, postures, signals, or actions it can be your own perspective that what you think of these certain acts, just don't get too selfy, first think of your own perspective that what you think about these then think neutralised about these acts.

Remember....
....Once you will learn this "art", you will never get in trouble because of it, it will only reverse affect the situation by helping you to get out of troubles and also for recovering bonds.

[[PAGE_BREAK]]

# PART III
# AFTERWARDS

[[PAGE_BREAK]]

# At The Very End...

At the very end of this book, I will like to conclude that writing this book was a very interesting journey to be in, it divined my knowledge of my mind. It enriched and refreshed my knowledge about my relation with my sibling. I hope you would like this book, I hope that it will be useful towards you and your sibling's relation, I hope this short but still a strong guide will be helpful, useful, and joyful for you. I have also created an actual website using Git Hub my self for my book writing career I will mention it in the about the author section so you can go there and get more information about my books, plans for the next goal, upcoming books etc... I really hope that you enjoy this "short-but-strong" guide, your support is the most valuable. And I hope that you will also become couraged to try my these type of "short-but-strong" guides series called "The Path To A Meaningful Life", we have already covered a book in that series called "The Hidden Power Of Discipline", I recommend that if you liked this book you should must read that book also so you can complete the goal of this series, to make our lives worth! To make our lives meaningful and worth that you are actually grateful to live in this amazing world and that this life was really meaningful and worth living to you. By the way I am still writing books live so this series can actually be completed. So, once more, that I will like to thank you to believe that this book was worth reading and to read it, and i hope that this book was enjoyable and useful to you.

So, one question remains....
....Is this the end?

# About the Author

Brothers, Sisters is the second book in his The Path To A Meaningful Life series, following his first book, The Hidden Power of Discipline. Through this series, he hopes to help readers develop a happier, kinder, and more meaningful life through simple yet powerful lessons.

Apart from writing, Sidharth enjoys programming, technology, science, gaming, music, and creating educational content. He believes that knowledge becomes valuable only when it is shared with others.
